rulings.note: corpus/env-vars.md:476 supports every part of the claim. It reads: "Unset, Claude Code defers all MCP tools by default, and loads them upfront instead when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points to a non-first-party host. ... `auto` loads upfront when tool definitions fit within 10% of context." Unset means all MCP tools are deferred, while auto loads them upfront under the 10% threshold, so on the default first-party path auto defers less than unset does, as the claim says. The only possible attack is the non-first-party host exception. The claim covers it by saying "by default", which is the doc's own wording, so it is a condition the claim already states, not a contradiction. No line on disk contradicts the claim, so the refuted verdict is wrong and confirmed is right.

caveats: Saturated. The gold and all 8 arms caught 7/7 false claims, and c03 came back untested everywhere. The only error in 9 runs is c10. With c10 set aside every run is perfect, so this run cannot tell Sonnet at medium from the gold. It bounds the cheap arms at this difficulty and does not rank them.

c10 label is contestable today. env-vars.md:476 now carries a host condition: unset loads tools upfront on a non-first-party ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, so there auto can defer more, not less. Both Opus medium runs refuted c10 on exactly that condition, which the production prompt tells skeptics to look for. The Opus high referee upheld confirmed, reading "by default" as covering it, and a review-round reviewer disagreed. Whether the condition was in the 2026-09-14 copy cannot be checked. The decision rests on that ruling. With c10 confirmed (the key, upheld by the referee) every run passes. With c10 set aside every run passes. With c10 refuted only the two Opus medium runs pass: the gold, both Opus low, both Sonnet high and both Sonnet medium runs each miss a false claim and fail. So this run cannot by itself justify moving the skeptics off the gold configuration.

One agent, 17 claims. The workflow spawns one skeptic per claim, while here one agent judged all 17. That lets claims that share evidence inform each other (c04/c11 cite the same lines with opposite claims; c01/c13, c07/c15 and c09/c12 overlap) and lets an agent read each page once. So the task is easier and cheaper than production. The costs are per 17-claim run, not per production round.
